about.title: Who we are
about.p1: We are a team of artists and educators formed in 2016 within the framework of the educational programmes of the Athens Epidaurus Festival. We design and deliver drama education programmes for children and adults, drawing inspiration from ancient drama as our starting point. Our experience at Epidaurus forms the foundation of our work, while we continually seek new ways to bring ancient drama closer to diverse audiences.
about.p2: Why ancient drama? Although its stories come from a distant world, the questions they raise remain relevant to us today and continue to resonate with contemporary life. This ongoing dialogue between past and present is what interests us and lies at the heart of our work. Through drama education, we aim to create a space where children and adults can engage with ancient drama, interpret it, and discover their own connections to it.

do.title: Discover what we do
do.intro: We design a «journey» through which children are gradually initiated, through individual activities, into the magical universe of each play.
do.frag3: connect invisibly to one another and unravel the thread of the plot of the
do.outro: in a fun and interactive way. The children reflect on the questions the text raises and are called upon to make decisions about how the story unfolds.

collectiveSpace.title: Collective shaping of the space
collectiveSpace.text: The visual-arts part is always the beginning of the programme, as it introduces the children to the story through the making of set objects that carry symbolic value, conveying meanings about the action to follow.

teacherInRole.title: Teacher in role
teacherInRole.text: The facilitator chooses the role suited to each moment, using a representative feature of that role (an object, a characteristic gesture, and so on). This technique sparks the students' interest, fosters their emotional engagement and creates the conditions for social interaction among the members of the group.

collectiveRole.title: Collective role
collectiveRole.text: The children collectively play the role of a single character. Each child is free to speak whenever they feel they can add something to the role, without any need for agreement between their views. At a later stage of the technique, the children can jointly arrive at a collective portrayal of a role that they all agree on to some degree, which also strengthens cooperation.

hotSeating.title: Hot seating
hotSeating.text: A child, or a facilitator in role, is questioned by the rest of the group in order to bring to light the character's motives, actions, perceptions, values and so on. This technique is best used at a crucial moment of the drama and makes it easier to reach a decisive choice, as it helps the children study human behaviour in depth.

mantleExpert.title: Mantle of the expert
mantleExpert.text: Without realising it, the children «know» what they don't believe they know. As experts, they are asked to investigate the data they are given, to solve riddles and to piece together clues, so that the world of the myth unfolds before them — along with the central question on which they are each time asked to take a position.

conscienceAlley.title: Conscience alley
conscienceAlley.text: The group splits in two and forms two facing rows, creating an alley. A facilitator or a child playing a particular role walks down the alley, while the other children voice the character's thoughts or offer advice about a decision they need to make. The character walking the alley, having heard the «voices of their conscience», then acts accordingly.

puppet.title: Puppet
puppet.text: The puppet is used as an independent dramatic character through which figures experiencing intense emotions, difficult situations, or moral dilemmas can be represented. Its small scale and material form create a safer and more indirect relationship between the children and the character, allowing them to approach fear, loss, guilt, or emotional suffering without being confronted with a realistic representation. The puppet can interact with the facilitator or with the children themselves, serving as a stimulus for dialogue, imagination, and emotional engagement. In this way, an object is transformed into the bearer of a vivid dramatic presence.

transformationOfMaterials.title: Transformation of materials
transformationOfMaterials.text: Mapping transforms space into a field of exploration and discovery. Children use a map to find their way, identify specific locations, and connect the physical environment with the dramatic world of the programme. Searching for particular places, objects, or elements of the story thus becomes part of a shared mission. The map may represent a real location or an imaginary world created through the dramatic action. In this way, moving through space becomes an active process of observation, discovery, and meaning-making.

audiovisualMaterial.title: Audiovisual material
audiovisualMaterial.text: This technique combines different media, such as light, shadow, projections, moving images, and sound, to create a distinctive dramatic environment. The individual elements do not function independently but are brought together to transform the space and create a world that could not be conveyed through stage objects alone. Images, sounds, and lighting can serve as landmarks, signal transitions, or guide children through different layers of the story. In this way, the space itself becomes part of the narrative, and the children do not simply observe an imaginary world but move through and explore it.

shadowTheatre.title: Shadow theatre
shadowTheatre.text: The technique of shadow theatre uses light and shadow to represent characters, events, and situations indirectly and symbolically. Through the screen, difficult or emotionally charged moments, such as death, loss, fear, or conflict, can be presented without being depicted realistically. At the same time, the abstraction of the image leaves room for children’s imagination and allows for the creation of poetic and symbolic imagery. The technique can also be used to portray mythical figures, transformations, and elements that transcend everyday reality.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.text: Η χαρτογράφηση μετατρέπει τον χώρο σε ένα πεδίο εξερεύνησης και ανακάλυψης. Τα παιδιά χρησιμοποιούν έναν χάρτη για να προσανατολιστούν, να εντοπίσουν σημεία και να συνδέσουν τον πραγματικό χώρο με τον δραματικό κόσμο του προγράμματος. Η αναζήτηση συγκεκριμένων τόπων, αντικειμένων ή στοιχείων της ιστορίας γίνεται έτσι μέρος μιας κοινής αποστολής. Ο χάρτης μπορεί να αφορά έναν πραγματικό χώρο, αλλά και έναν φανταστικό κόσμο που δημιουργείται μέσα από τη δράση. Με αυτόν τον τρόπο, η περιήγηση μετατρέπεται σε ενεργή διαδικασία παρατήρησης, ανακάλυψης και δημιουργίας νοήματος.

festival.findUs: Find us at the Athens Epidaurus Festival

1.text: When I came to pick him up, he said, “Mom, why did you come so quickly? I wanted to be the last to leave!” He kept talking about the experience the next morning too. You created a beautiful link between the experiences of parents and children.

2.text: They discovered the myth of Iphigenia in an interactive way and were gently introduced to ancient theatre. Later, as we discussed the performance and they shared their activity, it felt as though we had all experienced the same story.

3.text: We still talk about The Birds and what they would like to change before returning to the city. From The Bacchae, they remember the gods, while the masks and Dionysian wreaths they made still decorate their desks.

4.text: She happily described the crafts, the gold, the museum, and the conflict between Wealth and Poverty. The children found their own solution through solidarity, cooperation and sharing: “Wealth is family and time spent with friends.”

5.text: It is not just a place where I feel safe leaving the children during the performance. They genuinely look forward to it, leave having learned something, and afterwards we can all talk about what they experienced and what we saw.

6.text: The children talked about the symbols in the performance, the large dog they built from boxes, and the theatre itself. Afterwards, we could discuss it all together: me as a spectator, and the children through their own experience in the programme.

7.text: After the performance and over the following days, all three children shared, each in their own way and with great excitement, details from the activities. We talked a lot about the play and about how each of them understood the idea of Wealth.

8.text: It was a new and wonderful experience for all three of them. They gained meaningful knowledge about the play and the Theatre of Epidaurus and, with the educators’ guidance, worked beautifully together and stayed happily throughout the workshop.

9.text: Being able to watch the performance knowing that your child is creatively engaged in a welcoming environment, and then being able to share your experiences around the same theme afterwards, is incredibly valuable.

10.text: For a child to stay in the space for three hours, be completely happy, never complain, and actually look forward to going back is amazing to me. The work being done here is truly exceptional!
